The new test fails without the fix and passes with it. I also want to confirm the depth-2 half guards the frontier-expansion part specifically, so I'll disable just that part and rerun.
Now running fmt, workspace clippy, and the affected suites (`suite_usages` and `suite_semantic` with scheduled tests, the analysis library, the runtime extension tests, and the #3633 issue tests).

Still compiling. I'll wait for the completion notification before committing.

The broad test run is still going: `suite_usages` and `suite_semantic` with scheduled tests, the analysis library, the runtime extension tests, and the #3633 tests. I'll commit and push after it finishes.

So far:
- **#3633**: pinned the test fixture to LF line endings in `.gitattributes`. The two tests fail only on Windows, where checkout turns the fixture's line endings into CRLF and breaks a search string that contains `\n`.
- **#3679**: fixed both causes.
  - **C# access claim:** now published as a `Calls` claim instead of `ExceptionalControlFlow`, with the C# adapter bumped to v13. The CI failure now passes, and so do 970 C# and abort-route tests.
  - **Runtime tests:** the `FRONTIER` loop no longer contains a `+`, because the lowered abort route of a `+` gives the loop an exit. The expected node count changed from 4 to 6. All 14 runtime extension tests pass.
- **#3671**: `usage_graph` now links sites inside a merged node's other members to the node, including nodes reached at `depth > 1`. All 241 `usage_graph` tests pass. The new regression test fails if either part of the fix is removed.
13 of 7,341 tests failed. `--run-ignored all` also ran manual measurement tests that CI never runs. Checking each failure's message.
`origin/master` moved while I worked. The project rules forbid rebasing, and this repo's history uses merges, so I'll merge `origin/master` in.
Pushed. Now I'll post landing comments on the issues, close #3671 and #3679, and remove the in-progress labels.

I fixed all three CI failures and pushed to `origin/master` (at `6ace27427`, after merging in newer commits from `origin/master`). All the tests that failed in CI now pass locally, but I only ran them on Linux. I closed #3671 and #3679 and posted a comment on all three issues.

- **#3633** (`e15dea73b`): the two tests failed only on Windows. A Windows checkout turns the fixture's line endings into CRLF, so the test's search string (which contains `\n`) never matched. `.gitattributes` now pins that fixture to LF, as it already does for the #3087 fixtures. I couldn't run Windows; `git check-attr` confirms the rule applies.

- **#3671** (`abdf9f208`): `usage_graph` dropped edges from a C++ function declared in a header and defined in a `.cpp` file. The header prototype is the node's main declaration, and the per-depth lookup knew only that one, so references inside the `.cpp` body couldn't be matched to the node. The fix records the node's other declarations in that lookup and scans every file that declares a node reached at depth 2 or more.
  - At depth 2 the missing edges were also reported as `complete: true`.
  - A new test covers a header/`.cpp` free function at depth 1 and depth 2. Each assertion fails when its part of the fix is removed.

- **#3679** (`b5fa4c36d`):
  - **C# test:** I did not remove the claim that a property or element read can run getter, indexer, or type-initializer code, which the issue recommended. Removing it would hide real uncertainty: a read through a property with a getter body currently looks like a plain field read. Instead it is now filed as a possible call, the form C# already uses for user-defined operators, so it no longer marks every caller's exception path as unproven. The C# adapter version moves to v13, so stored C# results are rebuilt once. I did not run the DataFlowBench C# cases.
  - **Runtime tests:** these assumed behavior #3528 changed on purpose. The infinite-loop fixture had a `+` whose new exception edge let the loop exit, so its body is now `served = port;`. The node-count check changed from 4 to 6.

**Validation:** fmt and workspace clippy are clean. The affected suites passed with scheduled-only tests included (7,328 of 7,341). The 13 failures are tests marked ignored for other reasons: manual benchmarks, tests that need env vars or corpora, and one known Python gap. After the merge, the 375 targeted tests pass.

**Decisions for you:**
- Should a small C++ header/`.cpp` `usage_graph` check run on every push? The #3671 regression shipped because the only guard runs on the hourly schedule. The new test is scheduled-only like the tests next to it.
- I added changelog entries for #3671 and #3679 under 0.12.0 Fixed, following the #3633 entry.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- In Bifrost's semantic IR, the capability label on a gap decides how the solver treats it. The same "unknown user code" message counted against every caller's exception path when labeled as exception control flow, and only as a visible note when labeled as a call.
- The usage graph identifies each node by its main declaration. When one entity is declared in several files, every lookup from a single declaration back to its node has to cover all of them, not only the main one.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
pull, then fix & push #3680
The fix is on master, but every Hourly run since my push is still red. Checking what fails there.

#3680 needed no new code: it is the same Windows failure I fixed earlier this session in `e15dea73b`, which is already on master. That commit pins `issue_3633_basictests_reduced.cpp` to LF line endings in `.gitattributes`, exactly as the issue recommends. I pulled master, confirmed the fix, and closed #3680 with a comment citing the CI evidence. Nothing new to push.

**Confirmed on Windows CI:** the two #3633 tests no longer fail on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` in the two Hourly runs since my push (36164716518 on `6ace27427` and 36189439608 on `824ccad69`). The #3671 and #3679 tests no longer fail there either. The issue also suggests a broader LF rule for all C++ test fixtures; I did not add it, because the issue calls it a policy choice.

**Hourly CI is still red, from four other tests that fail on every platform.** No open issue tracks them:
- `issue_2189_2192_java_taint_propagation`: the Java exception-catch case is now incomplete ("must have complete value-flow evidence").
- `issue_2314_dataflowbench_kernel::java_kernel_templates_hold_on_the_policy_route`: the same Java case.
- `issue_2310_python_javascript_overwrite_branch_loop_baseline`: the JavaScript loop with `iteration++` is now `Complete` instead of its pinned inconclusive result.
- `issue_2314_dataflowbench_kernel::javascript_kernel_templates_hold_on_the_policy_route`: the same JavaScript case.

They first appear in the run on `6ace27427`, the merge that brought in my three fixes plus 34 upstream commits. My changes are unlikely to be the cause: they touched only C# lowering and the C++/C# usage graph, not Java or JavaScript. The likely source is upstream commits from the lint batch A work:
- `a3f06bf7f` "Decide JS/TS loose null and Boolean equality and prove primitive updates" matches the JavaScript failure.
- `b3a6d765b` and `b1cc6189f` changed how Java updates and guards are lowered, which matches the Java failure.

These attributions are not confirmed; I have not bisected. The failures may be tests that lag behind an intended change (the JavaScript one looks like that), or real regressions. The lint batch A work may belong to another agent, so I stopped here. I can bisect and fix them, or file an issue for whoever owns that work.
